blogs.title: The MODY Gray Zone: Navigating the Diagnostic Tension Between T1DM and T2DM in Young Adults
blogs.description: This post analyzes the common clinical pitfalls of treating MODY as Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes. It reviews the overlapping features of hyperglycemia and family history, discussing how to prioritize genetic testing when C-peptide and antibody results are inconclusive to avoid inappropriate insulin dependence or metformin monotherapy.

blogs.title: Precision in the Genomic Era: Interpreting Novel HNF1A Variants Without ClinVar Match
blogs.description: While pathogenicity databases are useful, this case illustrates the importance of ACMG guidelines for unknown variants. It explores how clinicians should evaluate novel HNF1A mutations using family segregation, bioinformatics scores (AlphaMissense), and structural context to avoid diagnostic exclusion.

blogs.title: Beyond the First Line: Why HNF1A-MODY Patients May Thrive on GLP-1 Agonists
blogs.description: Based on the successful treatment switch in the case, this post details the therapeutic nuance of HNF1A-MODY. It contrasts sulfonylureas versus GLP-1 receptor agonists, highlighting the advantage of utilizing GLP-1s to reduce hypoglycemia risk and preserve pancreatic beta-cell function over بست insulin therapy.

blogs.title: The Autonomic Clue: Using Sudomotor Testing to Support MODY Diagnosis
blogs.description: Often overlooked, autonomic dysfunction is a diagnostic consideration in early-onset diabetes. This post examines the clinical significance of sweat and sudomotor testing in differentiating MODY from autoimmune diabetes and discusses its sensitivities versus specific findings like the 'severely reduced conductance' in this patient.

blogs.title: Call for Diversity: Why Non-White Populations Need Better Representation in MODY Algorithms
blogs.description: This editorial addresses the case of an Asian patient and the limitations of global diagnostic calculators (e.g., Exeter calculator) based on Eurocentric populations. It advocates for updated epidemiological data to reduce under-diagnosis rates of MODY in Asian and other minority demographics.

blogs.title: The SGLT2 Paradox: Why SGLT2 Inhibitors Are a Risk in HNF1A-MODY
blogs.description: Although effective for most diabetics, SGLT2 inhibitors can carry specific risks in HNF1A-MODY due to SGLT2 inactivity in renal tubules. This post reviews the DASH mechanism and fungal infections/diabetic ketoacidosis risks to ensure safe pharmacologic choices for patients with MODY-like phenotypes.
